accepted.statement: The body-parser 2.3.0 package can be forced into a denial‑of‑service by sending a compressed request body that contains trailing bytes. It is pulled in transitively through express (and through the @modelcontextprotocol/sdk and express‑rate‑limit packages), so the vulnerable code can execute in the application. With a CVSS of 7.5 and a severity score of 31.4, this is a high‑impact issue; upgrade to body-parser 2.4.0 to remediate it.

The cors 2.8.6 package is flagged as a possible typosquat of the popular colors package because its name is within an edit distance of two. No vulnerability score is assigned, but the similarity could indicate a malicious substitution and the package is used transitively in the dependency graph. Review the intent and remove or replace the package to eliminate any risk.

The @hono/node-server 2.1.5 module can crash the process when an asynchronous WebSocket upgrade encounters an ECONNRESET error on the socket. It is included transitively via the @modelcontextprotocol/sdk, so the crash can affect the running application. With a CVSS of 5.3 and a score of 26.0, the issue is moderate severity; upgrade to @hono/node-server 2.1.6 to apply the fix.

The hono 4.13.13 package allows mount() and app.mount() to forward a path that can bypass middleware scoped inside the mount prefix. This vulnerability is reachable transitively through the @modelcontextprotocol/sdk (and also via @hono/node-server), so an attacker could reach protected routes. With a CVSS of 5.3 and a severity score of 25.3, upgrade to hono 4.13.16 to close the bypass.

The hono 4.13.13 package’s validator('form') skips validation for multipart/form-data requests that contain extra parameters. This flaw is reachable transitively via the @modelcontextprotocol/sdk (and also via @hono/node-server), potentially allowing malformed data to bypass input checks. With a CVSS of 5.3 and a score of 25.2, the issue is moderate; upgrade to hono 4.13.16 to obtain the corrected validator logic.

The @hono/node-server 2.1.5 module parses a backslash in the request path as a path separator, allowing an attacker to bypass path‑based access controls at a reverse proxy. It is pulled in transitively through the @modelcontextprotocol/sdk, so the bypass can be exploited in the application. With a CVSS of 5.3 and a severity score of 24.9, the vulnerability is moderate; upgrade to @hono/node-server 2.1.6 to fix the parsing issue.

fast-uri 3.1.8 can be tricked into interpreting a percent‑encoded URI scheme as a different scheme, leading to possible scheme spoofing. The vulnerable package is pulled in transitively through @modelcontextprotocol/sdk → ajv → fast-uri (see the two paths). With a CVSS of 6.1 and a Track SSVC score of 24.9, this moderate‑severity issue is reachable in the app. Upgrade fast-uri to at least 3.1.9 (and co‑upgrade ajv 8.20.0) to fix.
accepted.next_step: Upgrade fast-uri to 3.1.9 and align ajv version as recommended.

accepted.statement: hono 4.13.13 has a routing bug where RegExpRouter may skip wildcard middleware for certain routes and encoded line terminators, potentially bypassing security checks. The package is included transitively via @modelcontextprotocol/sdk directly and via @hono/node-server, as shown in the paths. With a CVSS of 5.3 and a Track SSVC score of 24.8, the issue is reachable in the app. Upgrade hono to 4.13.16 to resolve the problem.

The Dockerfile uses the base image node:22-slim by tag, which is unpinned and could be redirected to a newer, potentially vulnerable version. This occurs at line 1 of the Dockerfile, affecting the entire container build. With a Track SSVC score of 22.0, the lack of a digest makes the image supply chain mutable. Pin the base image to a specific sha256 digest (and avoid end‑of‑life tags).
accepted.next_step: Pin the base image to a specific digest.

accepted.statement: hono 4.13.13’s csrf() middleware fails to validate requests made with the text/ping content type used for hyperlink auditing, allowing CSRF bypass. The vulnerable version is pulled in transitively via @modelcontextprotocol/sdk (directly and via @hono/node-server). With a CVSS of 5.3 and a Track SSVC score of 21.3, the flaw is reachable in the app. Upgrade hono to 4.13.16 to obtain the fix.

The esbuild package (version 0.28.2) includes an install‑script that executes code during npm install. Although the package is not imported at runtime (reachability = not_imported), the script can run on any system that installs the dependency, posing a supply‑chain risk. With a score of 20 and an Ssvc of Track, it should be monitored for malicious behavior.
accepted.next_step: Monitor the install script and consider replacing the package if a safer alternative exists.

accepted.statement: The Dockerfile lacks a HEALTHCHECK instruction, meaning the container has no built‑in liveness probe and failures may go undetected. Trivy flagged this as misconfiguration DS‑0026 with a score of 12 and an Ssvc of Track, indicating it should be addressed. Apply the recommended fix by adding a HEALTHCHECK command to the Dockerfile as described in the Trivy report.
